you want a game with endless depth
you like managing crops and combat

citations.review_text: So i recently got Stardew Valley on Steam but I have over 100 hours playing this game on my Nintendo Switch so I promise I have some experience with this game lol. Anyways, to the review! So I absolutely love this game! It's a very easy game to pick up while still being a little complicated for more hard core players/fans late game. I has a wide range of different main quests like restoring the local museum, rebuilding the broken community center, and building close friendships with the local townspeople (and maybe starting a relationship with one). If you're hesitating on buying a farm-sim game there's a lot more to it than that, maybe you're more into mining, it's got that, or maybe you like exploring diverse locations, it's got that, or maybe you like slaying evil monsters, well it's got that too! So if you're looking for a fun, simple, and easy-to-play game, I promise you won't regret playing this one!!
PEAK so fun, fishing isn't as hard as folks say

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes combat elements alongside farming.

citations.review_text:
After years of owning this game on many different platforms, I love the amount of things in this game. Playing on steam for the first time is AMAZING! You learn the mouse and keyboard and the machanics, and if never played this game before, you can still experience the true beauty in what a game on steam should look like. The multiplayer is amazing, and the choices, festivals, and also the amount of money with sharing and seperating.

Should I even talk about the animals. The animals are SOO fun to hang out with, feed them, pet them, and all the materials. The amount of animal products, noises, and the kind hearted villagers that take care of animals are great. You start slow, starting with nothing, unless on the newest farm that starts you with 2 chickens, and 15 hay instead of 15 prsnips. Mining, Fishing, Foraging, Farming, and Combat are the 5 amazing skills to learn and master. Ginger island is beautifual, the mining materials are great, and the amount of house upgrades are awsome.

Getting married, having kids, cooking, cleaning, and clearing everything is fun. You start slow, and want to refund the game--then you face the community center. A ton of bundles, worth a bunch of value that give you prizes/rewards after completing. You start by meeting the wizard and start with the foragables of spring. 4 seasons--Spring, Summer, Fall, and Winter. I have never completed the game by getting perfection, but i still love how you have as much time as you want. Each day should last 15-20 minutes, and a year should take 37.33 hours which is plenty of time. I love this game, and will love it forever.

Stardew Valley is a game like no other, for one it's so addicting but other than that fact, the art style is adorable, the minimal story building gets me so excited and its a perfect mix of cosy farming game with a little bit of combat. I'd recommend this game to anyone and everyone, definitely in my top 3 games just for  how it makes me feel, it honestly helps with my anxiety to go into my little farm and just do some farming and mining. Love this game so much and always will!!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the beginning of the game as slow or hard before systems are understood.

citations.review_text:
Stardew Valley is one of those games that feels like a second home. It starts as a simple farming game, but the more time you spend in Pelican Town, the more you realize there’s so much more to do than just grow crops.

The freedom is what makes it special. You can spend your days farming, fishing, mining, exploring, decorating your farm, raising animals, or just getting to know the villagers. There’s no pressure to play a certain way, and somehow even small things like organizing your farm or catching a rare fish feel rewarding.

The characters are probably one of the best parts. Every villager has their own personality and story, and getting to know them makes the town feel alive. The little events, seasonal changes, and small details make it feel like an actual place instead of just a game map.

The amount of content is honestly crazy for a game made mostly by one person. There’s always something to work toward, whether it’s improving your farm, completing collections, unlocking areas, or just making your perfect little life.

The only downside is that the beginning can feel a bit slow, and if farming or relaxing games aren’t your thing, it might not hook you immediately. Some systems also take time to understand.

But once it clicks, it’s hard to put down. It’s relaxing when you want it to be, but it can also become surprisingly addictive when you start optimizing everything.

10/10. A cozy masterpiece with endless charm. A game where you can lose hundreds of hours and somehow still feel like you’re just getting started. ❤️
Very fun, hard at first, but when you get the hang of it, you will get addicted and lose track of time

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the fishing minigame is mildly annoying at first.

citations.review_text:
I love it. This game is a thing of beauty, and ConcernedApe should reasonably proud to have created such a wonderful game, and I'm proud that Stardew Valley has an amazing amount of players who are just, genuinely, some of the most hospitable people in the internet.

As for the review, I'd say that Stardew Valley HAS addicting music that just fits the mood of the game, I can wholeheartedly say that I never got bored and never found it as an annoyance. The fishing game is mildly annoying at first, then absolutely got me like fish on a bait when I saw the green bar become larger with a level up in fishing. Farming is profitable and chill, Sometimes I forget to pet my chickens, Sometimes I forget many things, but all in all... there's no rush, no "you need to do this to save the Republic" being enforced on you, and even in Youtube videos, I see that grandpa isn't harsh at the three years and actually thinks it's perfectly fine if as long as you're enjoying life, and that's so, incredibly heartwarming for me. Wish to see grandpa soon at his third year evaluation.
I absolutely love fishing in this game, if it wasn't for the sand fish I'd have finished the fishing tank part of the community center first, it's delightfully relaxing but also engaging.

claims.claim: Reviewers note the inclusion of arcade minigames like Journey of the Prairie King and Junimo Cart alongside the farming and combat systems.

citations.review_text:
Great game, cute stories, fun challenges!  This game has earned its reputation.  While it is a cozy farming sim, it also has combat elements and tests of skill that are very reminiscent of older arcade games.  It feels like an ode to old gameplay styles while appealing to modern audiences, with the fishing minigame, the in-game arcade games like Journey of the Prairie King and Junimo Cart, and the endless Skull Cavern levels.
Lots of replayability with the different farm layout options, or just keeping your farm running for however long you like.  
(The extensive modding community helps to increase the replayability too!)

I don't play video games but I have 300+ hours on this one. You can play it however you want to! It's a dating game, a sandbox world, a combat sim, a fishing game, a farming game, and a quest-based game all in one!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the early game as intensive, slow, and confusing, requiring players to figure out mechanics and planning.

citations.review_text:
At first this game did not hook me at all but as someone who likes to 100% games, I was determined to play it through fully. 

It's a well made game I'll give it to the dev. You can really tell that there's one brain behind it all. I love the details and the hidden secrets, the notes that you have to carefully read and solve mysteries, all the characters and their unique personalities, schedule, character development. While it seems like a chill game, you really need to pay a lot of attention and plan ahead. 

It's a grindy game and it takes quite some days to get the first achievement which in my opinion is pretty nice to not instantly get that dopamine kick. Rather it will reward you after you've worked hard enough. Most things are so expensive in this game, but I guess that's part of the grind. It's not easy and you have to figure out the best way to play this game, what to focus on, what sell price is the best, plan ahead based on day and season, and so on. Slowly you get rewarded in different ways. 

Early game is intensive, slow, and confusing. Mid game you start to get a hang of everything, and start the real money making and crafting grind, motivation to play can be on and off here. End game is kinda odd and confusing. That's when you finally get max level of everything and that's when you get the real "support" that I would have appreciate if I had them earlier. To me it makes no sense, especially the [spoiler]obelisks[/spoiler]. What is the point of having access to the "support" crafts/items after completing everything in the late game stage?

Overall, a fun game. It fits many play-styles like those who want to just farm and craft, those who like to fish, those who like to slay monsters. I wish you could save anytime during the day like the smartphone version, don't understand why that's not a thing on PC. But good game!

I have two copies of this, one on PS5 and the other on my PC. This game is everything. The work and care put into making it shows. There isn't a tutorial on playing, but your first farm isn't about min/maxing and optimisation. Take your time, learn the mechanics, talk to the villagers, delve into the lore. And have the Wiki open on your second monitor or phone.
